header.running_head: Exercising Caution when Issuing Fataawaa and the Sahabah (RA) who used to Issue Fataawaa

blocks.text: Umar (RA), Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) and Hadhrat Ali (RA) used to issue Fataawaa during the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ. [^1]

blocks.narrator: Hadhrat Fudhayl bin Abu Abdullaah bin Dinaar
blocks.text: Hadhrat Fudhayl bin Abu Abdullaah bin Dinaar narrates from his father that Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA), Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA), Hadhrat Umar (RA) and Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) were amongst those who issued Fataawaa during the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ according to what they heard from Rasulullaah ﷺ. [^2]
Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) Tells the People not to ask him Anything While Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) is Alive

Hadhrat Abu Attiyya Hamdaani reports that he was once sitting with Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) when a person came to ask him a question. "Have you asked anyone else?" Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) enquired. "Yes," the man replied, "I have asked Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA)." The man then informed Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) about Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA)'s reply. Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) gave a reply that contradicted that of Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) and then left. (When this was brought to the attention of Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA),) He said, "Do not ask me about anything when this great scholar is in your midst." [^3]
Those Who Issued Fataawaa during the Time of Rasulullaah ﷺ and the Time of the Khulafaa Raashideen

Hadhrat Sahl bin Abu Khaythamah reports that during the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ, three Sahabah (RA) from the Muhaajireen and three Sahabah (RA) from the Ansaar were authorised to issue Fataawaa. They were Hadhrat Umar (RA), Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA), Hadhrat Ali (RA) (from the Muhaajireen) and Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA), Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) and Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit (RA) (from the Ansaar). [^4]

Hadhrat Masrooq reports that from amongst the Sahabah (RA) of Rasulullaah ﷺ, those who issued Fataawaa were Hadhrat Umar (RA), Hadhrat Ali (RA), Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA), Hadhrat Zaid (bin Thaabit) (RA), Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA) and Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA). [^5]

blocks.narrator: Hadhrat Qabeesah bin Duayb bin Halhala
blocks.text: Hadhrat Qabeesah bin Duayb bin Halhala reports, "During the time of Hadhrat Umar (RA), Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit (RA) remained the chief authority of the judiciary of Madinah, as well as the chief authority of issuing Fataawaa, Qiraa'ah and dissolution of estates. He maintained this position during the time
Ibn Sa'd (Vol.4 Pg.157). Ibn Asaakir has reported a similar narration, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.5 Pg.77).
Ibn Sa'd (Vol.4 Pg.160). Abu Nu'aym has reported a similar narration in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.129).
